Flood Watch · screen board · v1 → v2

From a typed form to something you can hear and say

Real screenshots of the running prototype at phone size (390 × 844). Version 1 was tested in Round 1. Version 2 is what testers will use in Round 2. Scroll each row sideways.

Before: version 1 (Round 1)

Dark theme, small grey text, typing required, severity mostly by colour, and Dagbani that no fluent speaker had checked.

After: version 2, the main journey

One question per screen. Every instruction has a speaker button. Pictures, words and colour all say the same thing, so no one depends on reading or on colour.

Three languages

The same home screen in each language. Text is only half of it: a speaker's own recording of each phrase plays first, then the phone's voice for English, then GhanaNLP machine voice for Twi and Dagbani.

Research tools inside the app

Built for the before and after test, so results are recorded the same way in both rounds.

After Round 1: version 2.1

Five people tested on 11 October (three in Tamale, two in Accra). All five understood the app was for floods. The older testers needed help to find their way. One wanted to share her live location; another was afraid of being tracked at all. These screens respond to what they said.

What changed and why

The last column says where each change came from. Rows marked Round 1 come from what testers said; the rest come from the design review.

How voice and privacy work

Speaking to the app, and hearing it back

flowchart TD
  A[Person speaks in Twi or Dagbani] --> B[Phone records audio]
  B --> C{Reporting a flood?}
  C -- yes --> D[Saved as a voice note.
Neighbours hear it. Deleted after 24 h]
  C -- asking the helper --> E[GhanaNLP speech to text]
  E --> F[Translate to English]
  F --> G[Checked answers or Gemini]
  G --> H[Translate back]
  H --> I[GhanaNLP voice reads it aloud]

Flood reports never need speech recognition: the voice note itself is the message. This works in any language, including ones no AI supports.

What leaves the phone

flowchart LR
  P[Phone GPS] -->|stays on phone| M[Match to area list]
  M -->|yes or no + area name| S[(Flood Watch server)]
  S -->|area centre only| W[Open-Meteo rain forecast]
  S -->|never stored| X[Names · phone numbers · coordinates]

Votes are tied to a random code saved on the phone and then hashed, so one phone gets one vote without anyone being identified.
